US Federal Reserve lowers interest rates for third time this year

Published 2026-10-07 18:40 UTC

The US Federal Reserve has cut interest rates for the third time this year, lowering its benchmark rate by a quarter of a percentage point to a range of 3.25% to 3.5% amid growing concern about the health of the American jobs market.

The Fed's statement said downside risks to employment had risen, while inflation remained somewhat elevated. Two members of the Federal Open Market Committee dissented, preferring to keep rates on hold.

Speaking in Washington, the Fed chair, Jerome Powell, said policymakers would watch incoming data closely before deciding on a further cut in December. Wall Street rallied after the decision and the dollar weakened against the pound and the euro.

The cut brings the federal funds rate to a range of 3.75% to 4%, its lowest level since late 2022. The decision was widely expected by financial markets after a run of weak jobs data, including a monthly payrolls report that showed the slowest hiring in more than four years.

The central bank has come under political pressure to cut rates faster, with the White House repeatedly criticising the pace of easing. Fed officials have insisted that their decisions are based on economic data and that the bank's independence is essential for keeping inflation under control.

Economists said the decision reflects a shift in the Fed's priorities from fighting inflation to supporting employment. Inflation has fallen from its peak but remains above the 2% target, and some officials worry that tariffs on imported goods could push prices up again next year.

The cut is likely to influence other central banks. Lower US rates tend to weaken the dollar and reduce pressure on emerging markets with dollar debts. In the UK, analysts said the Bank of England may feel more able to lower its own rates if inflation continues to ease.

Stock markets in New York rose after the announcement, while the dollar slipped against the euro and the pound.
